LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD's top-level scope consists solely of standard metadata assignments: `pkgname`, `pkgver`, `pkgrel`, `pkgdesc`, `arch`, `url`, `license`, `depends`, `provides`, `conflicts`, `source`, and `sha256sums`. There are no command substitutions (e.g. `$(...)` or backticks) in any global variable, no `eval`, no `curl`/`wget`, and no piping to a shell. The `source` array is a single plain-quoted HTTPS URL to the project's own GitHub releases; the `$pkgname`/`$pkgver` interpolations inside it are ordinary variable expansion, not code execution.

Sourcing this file therefore performs no network access, no file writes, and no execution of external payloads. All actual work — `install` of the binary, LICENSE, README, CHANGELOG, and example config into `$pkgdir` — is confined to `package()`, which `makepkg --printsrcinfo` does not invoke and is out of scope for this gate.

Note for the later full audit (not a gate failure): the source is a prebuilt binary tarball pinned by a sha256 checksum, which is a normal -bin packaging choice; no issue affects this step.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>Top-level scope only assigns metadata; no code executes.</summary>
</security_assessment>
